title: Common Camellia: Ancient Camellias You Can Visit
meta_description: Nara's five-colour camellia sheds petal by petal, which most camellias refuse to do. Four camellias mapped, one Japanese and three Portuguese.
intro: A camellia is supposed to drop its flower whole, head and all, which is why samurai were said to dislike them. The four hundred year old tree at Byakugo-ji in Nara does not: it sheds petal by petal, and it opens red, white, peach, striped and variegated blossoms on the same plant, which is how it became one of the three famous camellias of the city. The other three mapped here are Portuguese, and that is not an accident. The mild wet north of the country suited Camellia japonica so well that Portuguese growers ended up exporting it back to the rest of Europe. Porto has traded on that since the nineteenth century; the pair in front of the church at Paranhos are six and a half metres tall with crowns ten metres across, which is not what most people expect from a shrub in a pot.
